findings.claim: The new comment declares that the loop asserts "every unconditional contract by name", but a fifth unconditionally-loaded contract (oo-quality-contract.md) is still asserted by a separate hand-written check immediately after the loop. The authoritative list of expected contracts is therefore split across two constructs while the comment claims one of them is complete, so the next person adding a contract has no single obvious place to register it and can extend the loop while believing coverage is total.

engine/runtime/opencode.go — reviewed the ten added lines (comment plus openCodeContractFromContent call, error branch, and append) and their surrounding context, including the following oo-quality load that reads from disk rather than the embedded asset.
engine/runtime/opencode_test.go — reviewed the replacement of the count-only bound and two name checks with a four-entry name loop, and the retained standalone oo-quality assertion that follows it.

engine/assets/anti-generic-design.md and skills/_shared/anti-generic-design.md — reviewed the rewritten advisory-scope paragraph describing gate.go frontmatter matching and the reversed provenance claim about .atl/skill-registry.md.

Findings are limited to maintainability defects that obscure behavior: a comment that overstates the completeness of a test's contract list, documentation that omits an injection path added in the same candidate, and a brittle positional comment reference.

findings.claim: The new contract is appended to the OpenCode prompt-config slice with no phase predicate, so on OpenCode every phase receives a contract the asset itself scopes to the UI-generating phases through its applies_to_phases frontmatter; the documentation edit shipped in the same candidate still states the narrow two-phase scope, and no test pins either scope, so the intended per-phase behavior of the newly wired contract is unproved.
proof_refs: engine/runtime/opencode.go:504 — the added append places the design contract in the same unconditional slice as the projection contract on line 494, with no phase filter anywhere in the added block.

engine/assets/anti-generic-design.md:9 — the rewritten advisory-scope note still limits injection to the phases that generate or refine UI/design and points at subagent_type matching in engine/gate/gate.go as the deciding mechanism.
engine/runtime/opencode_test.go:112 — the only added assertion for this contract is membership of its path in the contracts list; nothing asserts which phases receive it.

findings.claim: The replacement assertions match contracts by path string only, so they prove the entry is listed but never that the embedded asset bytes are the ones carried; pairing the anti-generic-design path with the wrong or empty embedded asset would still satisfy every assertion in this test, leaving the change vulnerable to the same listed-but-inert failure class it exists to close.
proof_refs: engine/runtime/opencode_test.go:114 — hasPromptContract is keyed on the contract path alone, so the loop over the four wanted names checks registration, not content.

engine/runtime/opencode.go:500 — the path literal and the embedded asset are independent arguments to openCodeContractFromContent, so nothing in the production call ties the registered path to the content it names.
engine/runtime/opencode_test.go:101 — prompt_config_hash is asserted to exist but never compared against an expected value, so a contract entry with wrong or empty content is not caught there either.

findings.claim: The rewrite promotes the frontmatter from documentation to the load-bearing binding while keeping the four-phase scope sentence, but this contract is also appended unconditionally to the OpenCode prompt config, so the strengthened claim now describes only one of two live injection paths and overstates how load-bearing applies_to_phases actually is at runtime.
proof_refs: engine/assets/skill-discovery-safety.md:9 — the added sentence keeps the four named phases while newly asserting that the frontmatter decides injection.
engine/runtime/opencode.go:494 — the surrounding unconditional appends show contracts entering the OpenCode prompt config without any applies_to_phases consultation.
